author: blu
body: To lerp gives linear interpolation between two integers scaled by a fraction expressed as numerator and denominator. To inverse-lerp gives where a value falls between two endpoints, returned as a scaled integer (0 to scale). To remap gives a value mapped from one range to another. To smoothstep gives a smooth Hermite interpolation between 0 and scale, with the input expressed as a fraction of the range. To step gives 0 below edge, 1 at or above. To int-sqrt gives the integer square root (floor). To int-pow gives integer exponentiation for small non-negative exponents (bounded to 0-20 to fit in 64-bit). To int-log2 gives the floor of log base 2 of a positive integer.
